summary: Every word may independently change whether it contributes, and an adversary can force comparison through its final character; direct prefix testing therefore matches the linear character-inspection lower bound.

optimality.argument: Consider words that match prefixes of s through their last inspected position. Changing the final character of any one word can change that occurrence from a prefix to a non-prefix without altering any other answer contribution. A correct worst-case algorithm must inspect all S word characters, while direct prefix comparisons inspect each at most once.

replacement_checks.evidence: Any uninspected character can be changed to make its word cease matching s while all other array entries remain unchanged.
Each startswith comparison reads at most the current word length, and the algorithm performs one comparison per occurrence.
Authored cases cover duplicate prefixes, exact equality, longer words, later-only substrings, every prefix length, no matches, and one-character inputs.
